The franchise maintains structural advantages through its private banking model, deep wealth management relationships, and expanding footprint in Metro New York. Executive leadership is watching deposit pricing discipline and net interest margin (the spread between interest earned on assets and paid on liabilities) as interest rates fluctuate.

Recent findings suggest that long-term shareholder value creation hinges on converting recent top-line momentum into higher return benchmarks across changing rate environments. Management remains committed to delivering long-term profitability targets that reflect full execution of its private banking business model.

Victor Wembanyama, NBA's dunk king, turns to the 'shunk' due to painful blister on hand

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (229 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Victor Wembanyama has found a latest way to shoot in order to give his hands a rest and prevent future blisters.
  • Recent findings suggest that it's called the "shunk," as San Antonio Spurs color commentator Sean Elliott put it.
  • Sources indicate that wembanyama showed off the "shunk" during the Spurs' 124-112 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Victor Wembanyama has found a latest way to shoot in order to give his hands a rest and prevent future blisters.

Recent findings suggest that it's called the "shunk," as San Antonio Spurs color commentator Sean Elliott put it. It's basically the 7-foot-4 Wembanyama "dunking" the ball through the basket like a jump shot.

Sources indicate that wembanyama showed off the "shunk" during the Spurs' 124-112 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday. The two-time All-Star posted 32 points, 11 rebounds and 1 "shunk.".

Sources indicate that "I'm not going to lie," Wembanyama noted afterward via ESPN. "Actually, I've had this blister forever, and it's killing me. And every time I dunk, it kills me. I've been dragging this blister for I don't know how long because of dunking. So, I did not [quit dunking], but if I can avoid it, I would.".

Industry observers note that through 16 games, Wembanyama leads all players with 72 dunks — Thursday's "shunk" was counted as a dunk by the NBA. The next closest is Giannis Antetokounmpo of the Miami Heat, who has 49. The Spurs star is on pace for 369 dunks this season, which would pass Rudy Gobert's record of 306 he amassed during the 2018-19 season.

Was the "shunk" the shortest jump shot Wembanyama has ever attempted?

"Yeah, for sure," he said. "Maybe ever.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cryptocurrency markets suffered another brutal sell-off on Friday, November 20, as a wave of selling across Wall Street spilled into digital assets.
    • As of early evening, Bitcoin (BTC -4.89%) had plunged 6.01% to $58,186.39, while Ethereum (ETH -7.59%) tumbled 9.03% to $1,596.72 and Solana (SOL -5.15%) declined 8.02% to $67.21.
    • According to recent reports, deteriorating investor risk appetite continued to weigh on cryptocurrencies Friday as concerns over interest rates, elevated valuations, and tighter financial conditions fueled a broad sell-off across global markets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By RJ Fulton – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:45PM EST.

    Cryptocurrency markets suffered another brutal sell-off on Friday, November 20, as a wave of selling across Wall Street spilled into digital assets. Bitcoin broke below the psychologically important $60,000 level, while Ethereum and Solana experienced even steeper declines as investors continued to retreat from riskier assets.

    As of early evening, Bitcoin (BTC -4.89%) had plunged 6.01% to $58,186.39, while Ethereum (ETH -7.59%) tumbled 9.03% to $1,596.72 and Solana (SOL -5.15%) declined 8.02% to $67.21. The latest losses come as major cryptocurrencies struggle to establish a bottom, with weakening liquidity and persistent selling pressure raising the prospect of fresh bear market lows.

    According to recent reports, deteriorating investor risk appetite continued to weigh on cryptocurrencies Friday as concerns over interest rates, elevated valuations, and tighter financial conditions fueled a broad sell-off across global markets. With the Nasdaq plunging more than 5%, investors appeared increasingly focused on raising cash and reducing exposure to riskier assets.

    Industry observers note that the simultaneous decline in stocks, gold, and cryptocurrencies suggests selling pressure is extending beyond individual markets. Rather than simply rotating capital between asset classes, investors appear to be reducing their overall risk exposure, leaving cryptocurrencies particularly vulnerable as liquidity conditions continue to deteriorate.

    Sources indicate that spot cryptocurrency ETFs suffered steep losses on Friday, mirroring the broader sell-off in digital assets. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT -5.87%) fell 5.87%, while the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC -6.16%) declined 5.97%. Meanwhile, the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA -9.16%) plunged 9.16%, reflecting Ethereum's particularly sharp decline.

    Bitcoin's break below $60,000 marks another significant deterioration in the cryptocurrency market's technical outlook. With Ethereum approaching $1,500 and Solana falling below $70, several major cryptocurrencies are now trading near levels that could determine whether the current bear market extends into 2027. If selling pressure persists, investors could see another round of latest lows before a sustainable recovery takes shape.

    Industry observers note that beyond price action, the broader withdrawal of capital from digital assets presents a more fundamental challenge. Bitcoin ETF outflows have reportedly exceeded $2.5 billion in 2026, while the simultaneous sell-off across stocks, gold, and cryptocurrencies suggests investors are prioritizing liquidity over risk-taking. Without renewed capital inflows, even sharp relief rallies may struggle to develop into sustained recoveries.

    Recent findings suggest that looking ahead, investors should watch whether Bitcoin can reclaim $60,000, Ethereum can recover above $1,800, and Solana can establish support above $70. Improving ETF flows, stabilizing prices, and a recovery in broader financial markets would provide more convincing evidence that conditions are improving. Until then, the combination of weakening demand and unfavorable macroeconomic conditions leaves cryptocurrencies vulnerable to further declines heading into year-end.

    #16392. Industry News: SpaceX Prepares to Spend $2.8 Billion on Gas Turbines. Here’s What That Much Natural Gas Demand Means for Pipeline Investors.

    Industry News: SpaceX Prepares to Spend $2.8 Billion on Gas Turbines. Here’s What That Much Natural Gas Demand Means for Pipeline Investors.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, when SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%) went public in June, it disclosed $2.8 billion in purchase commitments for gas turbines and related equipment in its IPO prospectus.
    • That massive investment in behind-the-meter (BTM) natural gas connections, which generate electricity on the customer's side of the electric meter rather than going through an energy provider, is a bright green flag for the natural gas market.
    • An easy way to profit from that secular trend is through midstream pipeline companies, which deliver the natural gas to those data centers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Leo Sun – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:55PM EST.

    In a recent development, when SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%) went public in June, it disclosed $2.8 billion in purchase commitments for gas turbines and related equipment in its IPO prospectus. SpaceX is purchasing those turbines to power its own data centers and factories.

    That massive investment in behind-the-meter (BTM) natural gas connections, which generate electricity on the customer's side of the electric meter rather than going through an energy provider, is a bright green flag for the natural gas market. U.S. data centers already generate over 40% of their electricity from natural gas, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). That percentage could continue to rise as the cloud and AI markets expand.

    An easy way to profit from that secular trend is through midstream pipeline companies, which deliver the natural gas to those data centers. Pipeline operators charge companies "tolls" to use their infrastructure, so they're well-insulated from volatile commodity prices. Instead, they simply need the resources to keep flowing through their pipes to generate stable profits. Most pipeline companies also return lots of cash to their investors through high dividends and distributions.

    As demand for natural gas rises, pipeline companies will need to expand their infrastructure to handle the increased volumes. Those investments could compress their near-term margins, but they'll support their long-term growth. Let's see which of these pipeline operators will benefit the most from the rapid growth of the cloud infrastructure and AI data center markets.

    The Williams Companies (WMB -2.75%) operates more than 32,000 miles of pipeline across 24 states. It owns Transco, the largest natural gas pipeline in the U.S., which connects the Gulf Coast to the Atlantic seaboard. Its pipelines handle roughly a third of all natural gas produced in the United States.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that unlike more diversified pipeline companies, Williams generates most of its revenue by gathering, processing, storing, and transporting natural gas. A smaller percentage of revenue comes from natural gas liquids (NGLs), crude oil handling services, and electricity generation.

    In a recent development, from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Williams' EPS to grow at a 12% CAGR. It still looks reasonably valued at 26 times next year's earnings, and it could command an even higher valuation if the data center market heats up again.

    Industry observers note that williams has raised its dividend annually over the past nine years, and it's paid continuous dividends for the past 52 years. It presently pays a forward yield of 3.2%, and its low payout ratio of 82% gives it ample room for future dividend hikes.

    Sources indicate that energy Transfer (ET -2.62%) operates more than 140,000 miles of pipeline across 44 states. It transports crude oil, natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), and other refined products through its pipelines. It also exports NGLs through its marine export terminals.

    TXSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Energy Transfer's pipelines transport about 30% of the natural gas produced in the United States. It generates only approximately 40% of its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) from natural gas, which makes it less of a direct play on natural gas than Williams. Still, Energy Transfer is more exposed to that market than many of its peers.

    Sources indicate that unlike Williams, which operates as a traditional corporation, Energy Transfer is a master limited partnership (MLP) that treats its investors as partners rather than shareholders. MLPs pay distributions -- much of which are classified as a "return of capital" for more tax-efficient returns -- rather than traditional dividends. That strategy enables it to pay a high forward yield of 7.2%, but its investors must file an additional K-1 form (for MLPs) with their taxes each year.

    According to recent reports, from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Energy Transfer's earnings per unit (EPU) to grow at a 13% CAGR. It trades at just 12 times next's year's EPU, and that low valuation should limit its downside even if the cloud and AI markets cool off over the next few years.

    Credo Technology Group vs. Western Digital: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:57PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Credo Technology Group ›.
    • The race for faster data processing is pushing infrastructure to its limits, forcing a choice between specialized connectivity and massive storage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:57PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Credo Technology Group ›.

    The race for faster data processing is pushing infrastructure to its limits, forcing a choice between specialized connectivity and massive storage. You might be deciding between Credo Technology Group (CRDO -15.20%) and Western Digital (WDC -12.02%) for 2027.

    In a recent development, credo provides high-speed connectivity solutions that enable artificial intelligence data centers to communicate efficiently, while Western Digital is a global leader in both hard disk and flash storage. While they operate in different niches, both are essential players in the scaling of cloud infrastructure. This comparison evaluates which stock offers the best path for long-term growth.

    It has been revealed that credo Technology Group specializes in high-speed copper and optical interconnect solutions designed for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company sells products like Active Electrical Cables and optical components to hyperscale operators and system vendors. It has established key partnerships with Oracle (ORCL -8.48%) and Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) to enhance connectivity for dual-architecture systems.

    The demand for faster semiconductor stocks has significantly boosted its financial performance. In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached nearly $1.6 billion, representing a 165.1% increase over the previous period. This expansion led to a net income of roughly $538.3 million and a net margin of about 33.8%.

    Recent findings suggest that as of its May 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, meaning the tech giant carries no debt relative to shareholder equity. Its current ratio is approximately 10.2x, indicating a strong ability to cover short-term debts with current assets. In the fiscal year ended May 2, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $407.0 million, though stock-based compensation represented roughly 39.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    Industry observers note that western Digital designs and supplies essential data-storage solutions for enterprises and hyperscale cloud providers. Its product portfolio includes both hard disk drives and flash-based storage serving a global market across Asia and the Americas. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk, with three individual clients accounting for 16%, 15%, and 13% of total net revenue in its latest annual report.

    Industry observers note that in the 12 months ended Oct. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $14.5 billion, representing a 43% increase compared to the prior year. Net income for this period was nearly $10.0 billion, which indicates a net margin of roughly 69.2%. This performance suggests a robust recovery in cloud storage demand, which now accounts for nearly 89% of its net revenue.

    Recent findings suggest that on its July 2026 balance sheet, the company shows a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.1x, meaning total debt is low relative to equity. The current ratio stands at approximately 1.3x, measuring how well the company meets its short-term financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended July 3, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $3.5 billion, representing operating cash flow minus capital expenditures.

    In a recent development, credo Technology Group faces intense competition from larger industry peers like Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%), Marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%), and Astera Labs (ALAB -14.77%). The organization also deals with geopolitical risks due to its reliance on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company for all semiconductor manufacturing. Furthermore, it manages previously flagged intellectual property litigation with Marvell Technology, which was recently resolved via a settlement.

    In a recent development, western Digital must navigate risks associated with its complex strategic initiatives, such as the 2025 separation of its former flash business unit. It competes directly with other storage manufacturers like Seagate Technology Holdings (STX -12.35%) and providers of alternative storage technologies. Additionally, the company relies on a limited supply base for critical components, leaving it exposed to potential global supply chain disruptions.

    Western Digital is cheaper, trading at a lower Forward P/E for future earnings estimates and a lower P/S ratio based on sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    I'd go with Credo Technology, a organization whose sales have more than doubled year over year for seven straight quarters. AI data centers run on thousands of chips that need to share data swiftly, and Credo is a key player that makes the connections between them.

    Management expects sales to grow more than 85% this fiscal year, and Credo is also very profitable, turning about half of its sales into adjusted profit. It's also moving into optical products that carry data farther than its copper cables can, and management expects them to bring in more than $600 million this fiscal year. The stock fell after its recent earnings report, as investors worried that a few significant customers make up most of its sales, but Credo added another big customer in its latest quarter.

    To its credit, Western Digital's hard drives store much of the data AI creates, and its profit has jumped. But rival Toshiba is reportedly doubling its hard drive capacity, which could pull prices down. For long-term investors, Credo pairs fast growth with strong profits, and it has a front-row seat as AI data centers get bigger. With plenty of cash on hand, it can keep investing in fresh products for years to come.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Neocloud manufacturer CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    Recent findings suggest that recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    Chatterjee noted CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    It has been revealed that "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    According to recent reports, after a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    Industry observers note that over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    Sources indicate that meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell stated.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    According to recent reports, powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that in a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he stated.

    Industry observers note that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    In a recent development, overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the company if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he noted. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    Sources indicate that "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," remarked Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Ebiefung – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

    Few businesses exemplify American business success more than Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%). Since its founding in the late 19th century, the multinational beverage maker has expanded globally to serve billions and become one of the world's most recognized brands. Investors have profited substantially along the way, and this shows little sign of stopping.

    Over the last 12 months alone, shares have jumped by an impressive 35%, substantially outpacing the S&P 500's return of just 8% over the same time frame. This is a big deal for a company that is already large and mature. Let's dig deeper into the pros and cons of Coca-Cola to decide if the company still has millionaire-maker potential.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, to understand Coca-Cola's appeal, it can pay to listen to the philosophy of one of its biggest backers, Warren Buffett. His Berkshire Hathaway portfolio owns a whopping $38.4 billion worth of Coca-Cola stock, making it his third-largest bet behind American Express and Apple.

    According to recent reports, buffett likes to invest in companies with simple and easy-to-understand business models that enjoy a strong economic moat. A moat is a competitive advantage that protects a tech giant's market share against competition and allows it to enjoy stable or elevated pricing power. Coca-Cola is arguably the quintessential example of this type of business.

    You can walk into a convenience store or restaurant practically anywhere in the world and find Coca-Cola's flagship beverage Coke (or one of its many subbrands like Sprite, Fanta, and a variety of localized options).

    In a recent development, the company's ubiquitous shelf space has created unparalleled habit creation among its consumers, which is something upcoming rivals will struggle to disrupt, even if they manage to create better-tasting products. This advantage also makes Coca-Cola's sales remarkably recession-resistant. It has allowed the company to protect its margins amid soaring global inflation in raw materials like aluminum and sugar.

    Sources indicate that coca-Cola's gross margins have hovered around 60%, despite the soaring prices for its products. This suggests the organization is passing on the vast majority of inflation to consumers, while protecting its own profitability.

    KO Gross Profit Margin data by YCharts.

    Coca-Cola isn't without some long-term challenges. The firm is already a global brand name, and that means there is very little room for organic growth. Management will be increasingly tempted to rely on price increases to juice investor returns. While the company's gross margin of over 60% was easy to justify back when a 12-pack cost $4.00, it is much harder to stomach when prices have doubled, and more American families are struggling to make ends meet.

    According to recent reports, soda prices have far exceeded the U.S. inflation rate, despite boasting a disproportionately middle- and lower-income consumer base. It's hard not to wonder if this situation is as sustainable as it may look on the surface.

    Over the long term, there could be a generational shift away from brand-name soft drinks as people become more comfortable buying lower-cost store brands from major retailers like Walmart, which offers alternatives like Sam's Cola and Twist Up.

    Coca-Cola's recent performance is impressive, and its strong moat can help set the company up for more market-beating growth over the long term. That remarked, with a market cap of $422 billion (in a mature industry with relatively little room for organic growth), Coca-Cola's days of explosive millionaire-making growth are likely behind it. Shares are also somewhat expensive at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 28.

    Investors who buy the stock now should look at it as a safer alternative to more speculative opportunities like generative AI. The manufacturer's dividend (right now boasting a yield of 2.21%) will likely represent a sizable percentage of its long-term returns.

    • Recent findings suggest that pfizer (PFE -0.51%) faces a large patent cliff, and investors worry it won't be able to offset the revenue it loses as older drugs face generic competition.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Pfizer ›.

    Recent findings suggest that pfizer (PFE -0.51%) faces a large patent cliff, and investors worry it won't be able to offset the revenue it loses as older drugs face generic competition. That's a problem, but the drugmaker is aware of it and is making important strides in its efforts to address the issue. The substantial story, however, is that this issue is pretty normal for a drug organization.

    In fact, revenue from recently debuted and acquired drugs rose 32% in the third quarter of 2026. That shows the pharmaceutical giant's efforts are bearing fruit. But there's more reason to be excited, including the firm's strong balance sheet, its large dividend, and management's commitment to continue paying that dividend. Here's what you need to know.

    It has been revealed that one of the biggest worries about Pfizer is its upcoming patent expirations. Two big ones are Eliquis in 2028 and Vyndamax in 2031. But patent expirations are a normal part of the pharma sector. And research and development efforts in the highly technical and intensely competitive healthcare sector don't always align perfectly with a company's patent expiration schedule. It's just a fact of life.

    In a recent development, the 32% revenue growth Pfizer achieved from released and acquired products is evidence that the tech giant is seeing some success in its efforts to address the issue. And it sets up three more reasons to consider buying the stock.

    Pfizer ended the third quarter of 2026 with $1.8 billion in cash and $12.4 billion in short-term investments. That gives the company significant firepower to support its business through this patent-expiration cycle. In fact, the company's cash hoard is slightly higher than at the start of the year, so it isn't rapidly burning through its savings.

    Despite the organization's results with upcoming drugs and its financial strength, investors are deeply negative on Pfizer's stock. That's highlighted by its huge 6.1% dividend yield as of this writing. To put that yield into context, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) yields roughly 1.1%, and the average pharma stock yields 1.3%.

    The negativity highlighted by the elevated yield is echoed by more traditional valuation metrics. Pfizer's price-to-sales and price-to-book ratios are below their five-year averages. And while the price-to-earnings ratio is elevated, it is largely due to one-time charges. Looking at the whole picture, Pfizer's stock looks attractively priced.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, given the lofty yield, Pfizer is likely to be most appealing to dividend-focused investors. But right now earnings aren't covering the dividend. That's not a great sign, but one-time charges are part of the glitch. If you look at cash flow, the manufacturer can still support the dividend. That's highlighted by a cash dividend payout ratio of roughly 85%. While a lower number would be better, there's still some room for adversity. And don't forget about the company's large cash pile.

    Both of these facts help support management's strong backing of the dividend. Indeed, one of Pfizer's key capital priorities is to "maintain and grow our dividend." Obviously, the organization's priorities could change, but it wouldn't make a statement like that if the board of directors wasn't on board with protecting the dividend.

    Sources indicate that at the end of the day, Pfizer is facing very real headwinds today. But it is an industry-leading tech giant with a long history of success. If history is any guide, it will muddle through this difficult period. The success it is having with new drugs, its financial strength, attractive valuation, and dedication to its large dividend are all strong reasons for investors to take a deep dive before 2026 is over. If you wait too long, the opportunity here may pass you by.

    • Industry observers note that kelly Iko: Victor Wembanyama, with a sliiiight edge over Luka Dončić.
    • At this check-in, I have to go with Dončić after a month full of a variety pack of stepback 3s.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With the NBA season hitting the one-month mark, let's hand out some early awards! Who has been the most valuable player so far? The best rookie? The league's breakout star? Our writers weigh in with their picks.

    Industry observers note that kelly Iko: Victor Wembanyama, with a sliiiight edge over Luka Dončić. Of players that have registered at least 300 minutes so far, the Spurs are 42.5 points per 100 possessions better with him on the floor, the most impactful in the league by some distance. (San Antonio looked like a fish out of water earlier this week when he was on the bench vs. Detroit.) He's also realized that, at 7-foot-4, his rim presence should be consistently weaponized. Per Second Spectrum, Wemby logged 65 alley-oop dunk attempts all of last season; he's at 40 before Thanksgiving. Add this growth to his continued defensive wizardry, along with taking care of the ball and improving as a creator, and you have yourself a solid argument.

    (Dillon Minshall/Yahoo Sports illustration).

    Steve Jones: Luka Dončić. At this check-in, I have to go with Dončić after a month full of a variety pack of stepback 3s. That's 38 points a night with defenses attempting to throw multiple schemes at him and it just hasn't mattered a ton yet. Combine that with him "doing his job" on defense, with more activity on switches and rotations; he's a significant reason why the Lakers are at the top of the West.

    Dan Devine: Luka Dončić. I'm with Steve, give me the league's leading scorer, the reason the Lakers have been consistently vying for the No. 1 offense in the NBA, and the driving force behind an L.A. team that couldn't get out of the first round last year being neck-and-neck with the conference champion Spurs and East-leading 76ers for the league's best record. For more information, consult your local library:.

    Nekias Duncan: Victor Wembanyama. I don't think you can go wrong with Dončić or Wembanyama, honestly, but 28-12-3-1-4 on 62 true shooting is absolutely nuts. Wemby's dunking everything in sight, making teams pay when they send help — his assist rate has risen, while his turnover rate has dropped from last year — and he's pretty easily been the most destructive defender in basketball this year. The "off" portion of Wemby's on-off numbers are insane, but I'd redirect to the "on" portion — the Spurs are outscoring teams by over 28 points per 100 possessions with him on the floor.

    Industry observers note that duncan: Cameron Boozer. With all due respect to Yaxel Lendeborg and Darius Acuff Jr. (don't let them boo you, significant dawg), I'll also be rolling with Mr. Boozer. I've been enamored with his processing speed and versatility all year long. He attacks or passes ahead of tilted defenses at a high level already. He's also showcased a willingness to let it fly from deep, a necessary buffer while he gets comfortable with his inside-the-arc work (he's converting 60% of his 2s over his last six games) against bigger players.

    According to recent reports, jones: Cameron Boozer. Rookie of the Year is going to continue to heat up as this season goes on, but Boozer's versatility offensively has delivered consistent impact for the Grizzlies. His ability to playmake fits right in with their identity: he can punish switches, and he can make plays on the short roll. There has rarely been a game where he hasn't left an imprint for a Grizzlies team that just keeps winning.

    It has been revealed that devine: Yaxel Lendeborg. I'm firmly on the record as very on-board for Boozer, who became the second-youngest player in NBA history to record a triple-double, but I'll give a shout out to Lendeborg. Yes, it's been a pretty brutal week for him, and for the Warriors as a whole, since Stephen Curry went down. But what he showed in his first dozen games as a pro was truly eye-opening. Coming out of Michigan, the book on Yaxel was that, as a 24-year-old super-duper-senior, he'd have the experience, toolkit and physical maturity to be able to immediately fill a role in the league. I'm not sure anyone saw that role being "guy who can average an efficient 20-plus a night on high usage, and help elevate a team that just about everybody thought was drawing dead." That might not last forever, especially if Steph's absence stretches. But for the first month, it was an exceedingly pleasant surprise.

    It has been revealed that iko: Darius Acuff Jr. I'm not going to punish Acuff for being born into the Kings family. I'm also not going to magnify his low shot-making efficiency or assist-to-usage ratio in Sacramento. This kid is an absolute terror with the ball in his hands, averaging 26.2 points, 7.0 assists and 3.6 rebounds a night. In spite of Sacramento. You wanna know the list of folks to achieve benchmarks like that as a rookie? Wilt. Kareem. Jordan. Oscar Robertson. Elvin Hayes. Darius. His feel for the game, creation and scoring versatility is there — the rough edges will smoothen out as time goes on.

    In a recent development, jones: Memphis Grizzlies. While the Sixers keep finding ways to win as they figure it out, and while the Lakers are at the top of the West, and the Wolves have stayed steady without Anthony Edwards, the Grizzlies being one game out of the top is something few saw coming. They are 8-0 on the road, which is not just the best road start in franchise history, but the longest road winning streak in franchise history. Let that sink in.

    Duncan: Houston Rockets, if for no other reason than to save you all from the massive victory lap I'd like to take over the Grizzlies. It's not a surprise that the Rockets are a good team; the way they've been good is simply not what I had on the bingo card. They have the league's best offense and a top-five half-court unit to boot — a notable shift from last year (7th overall, 19th in the half-court). This largely hasn't been the Kevin Durant show; this is the second lowest scoring (21.3) and lowest shot-taking (13.3 attempts) season of his career. The growth and empowerment of Alperen Şengün and Amen Thompson, the confidence and shot-making of Jabari Smith Jr. (career-best 38.8% from 3), and the return of the steady-handed Fred VanVleet has led to a more efficient, free-flowing offense.

    In a recent development, iko: Houston Rockets. They have very quietly made a compelling case for being a top-5 team in the NBA. VanVleet's return has come with less control than he's accustomed to, but when you're converting shots at the highest efficiency of your career, who cares about usage rates? Smith is more confident in his in-between game and still has a knack for timely momentum-shifting splashes — as well as an unheralded five-position defensive skill set. They are second in offense and seventh in defense, don't turn the ball over, obliterate opponents on the offensive glass and still have a healthy Durant. Why couldn't they stick around until June?

    Industry observers note that devine: Portland Trail Blazers, in part because I'm an incorrigible shill who wants to deliver a ruthless plug for the substantial story he just wrote on Damian Lillard, and in part because I'm not sure anybody saw Portland sitting at 10-5 with a top-10 defense heading into opening night. Micah Nori's done a sensational job, Donovan Clingan and Toumani Camara look like bona fide linchpins, Jrue Holiday is always just what the doctor ordered, and Scoot Henderson even broke out against the Bucks on Thursday. Get Ja Morant back on the court, and Portland might just have a stew goin'.

    Devine: Toronto Raptors. It's not a shock to me that they are 5-10, given the myriad injuries they've suffered — most notably, obviously, getting just two games out of Kawhi Leonard before he went down with amorphous, ill-defined knee woes that, in a recent report by the great Michael Grange of Sportsnet, evoked the phrase "mystery condition." (Who could have foreseen this?!?) I do find it disappointing, though, that a team that won 46 games with the point differential of a 50-win squad and a top-seven defense last season — without Leonard — has so often looked so feckless this season … and that it's a combined 0-8 against teams with .500 or better records, getting blitzed by 11.5 points per 100 possessions against opponents with top-10 net ratings. Maybe, with better health, the Raptors will turn things around. Right now, though, even given the absence of their substantial-ticket offseason acquisition, they seem disappointingly unserious.

    Sources indicate that iko: Charlotte Hornets. There's no way you could have convinced me the Hornets would be 28th in net rating a week before Thanksgiving. I know the injuries to Kon Knueppel and Coby White have delayed what should have been a smooth start. But there's just something off about them when you watch, a level of disharmony and disjointedness that shouldn't be there this early in a season. Their collapse this week on the road in L.A., a game in which they led quite comfortably by 18 points deep into the second half, was embarrassing. The erasure of Brandon Miller, who has suddenly turned into a hybrid of Monta Ellis and J.R. Smith, is also jarring. Charles Lee has quite the tall task on his hands.

    Industry observers note that duncan: Utah Jazz, by default. Injuries have simply derailed this group. The playmaking and screening chops of Jusuf Nurkić were missing to begin the year, an underrated hit to what the Jazz want to establish. More pressing, they've had to navigate absences from Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen. It's led to an offense that has felt rudderless at times — and easy to switch against — paired with a defense that isn't good enough to hold things together. I simply didn't think this would be a three-win team a month in.

    Jones: Cleveland Cavaliers. Per NBA.com, they are the No. 4 scoring team in the league (118.3), boasting the No. 5 offensive rating in the league (117.5), and it doesn't feel like it at all. For a team with this level of firepower, with the added bonus of continuity after an Eastern Conference finals run, the drink has felt flatter than usual. The Cavs likely just need a quick chat with momentum to turn things around, but I had high expectations for this group to take off or figure things out quickly. It has felt stuck in the middle to me.

    It has been revealed that iko: Paul George. If this is intended for younger players, I apologize, but I'm in complete awe of what 36-year-old is doing right now in Boston. He's played next to Jayson Tatum for only a month, but their synergy screams of a lifelong partnership. He's still firing off eight 3s a night while converting them at the highest clip of his career; still serving as an effective secondary creator, scorer and connective tissue for MazzullaBall; and still one of the premier contest-without-fouling wings around. This was supposed to be a puzzling Celtics transaction, remember? Not acquiring a player nearing 40 who's still producing at a top-25 level. Color me shocked.

    In a recent development, jones: Davion Mitchell. Just the term breakout star had me in a headlock; I wanted to go with KAT, but he's already broken out, Cooper Flagg has taken a leap, Franz Wagner is scoring and playmaking, and LaMelo Ball is playing defense. I'm going with Mitchell, leaning on the breakout portion of the program. He's been dynamic in transition and in pick-and-roll, finding his way into the paint consistently. The on-ball pressure remains tremendous and he's knocking down 3s. He's been exactly what the Heat have needed.

    Recent findings suggest that duncan: Cedric Coward. (Davion Mitchell is such a tremendous shout!) Coward has simply been awesome for the Grizzlies to start the year. He's shooting the leather off the ball (45.2% on 5.2 attempts from 3), the drives have more juice, the passing has perked up, and he continues to add value as an offensive rebounder. On the other end, he's putting together a legitimate All-Defense campaign while consistently taking on tough assignments. As of this writing, opposing offenses are generating under 0.8 points per possession whenever Coward defends a ball screen (0.76), a handoff (0.76), or an off-ball screen (0.55). There's a reason the Grizzlies have been nearly 15 points better per 100 possessions with him on the floor.

    Sources indicate that devine: Holy crap, none of you guys remarked Ty Jerome? OK, then: Ty freaking Jerome!

    There are five players in the NBA this season averaging at least 25 points and five assists per game on .600 true shooting, and Ty Jerome is the only one of them that 99% of NBA fans couldn't pick out of a lineup. (The other four: Luka, Giannis, Tyrese Maxey, Jamal Murray.) Sickos who do this for a living might have been aware that the eighth-year pro out of Virginia could be capable of this sort of production given health and opportunity, but it's certainly come as a shock to just about everybody else — including opponents of the Grizzlies who might've come into the season expecting things to be sweet only to find themselves on the business end of a steady diet of impossible floaters and 30-foot pull-up bombs. Memphis has been one of the best stories in the league this season, and its low-profile, high-octane point guard has been one of the biggest reasons why.

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:29PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than BigBear.ai ›.

    Industry observers note that choosing between these specialized AI plays requires balancing high-stakes government work against commercial data engineering growth. Investors must decide if BigBear.ai (BBAI -8.67%) or Innodata (INOD -8.91%) better suits their portfolio needs.

    Sources indicate that bigBear.ai provides complex decision intelligence tools for federal and defense agencies, while Innodata helps major tech firms train generative AI systems. Both companies operate in the rapidly evolving world of artificial intelligence but serve different markets. This comparison examines their financial health, customer concentration, and valuation to help you decide which stock fits your strategy.

    BigBear.ai offers decision intelligence solutions that combine data from different sources to help leaders make faster choices. It serves critical sectors like national security, cybersecurity, and global supply chains. According to its latest annual report, a specific contract accounted for nearly 51% of consolidated revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

    Sources indicate that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $142.1 million. This represented a revenue growth decline of approximately 1.5% compared to the prior period. The organization reported a net loss of roughly $180.2 million during this same time frame.

    Following its early 2026 debt conversion, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.0x, meaning the tech giant carries virtually no debt relative to its equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, is close to 1.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was negative at nearly $46.3 million.

    Innodata operates as a global data engineering firm that prepares and evaluates data for large-scale AI systems. The firm serves several high-profile technology leaders, with one customer in its digital data solutions segment accounting for nearly 58% of total revenue in 2025. This focus on the best small cap tech stocks in the data sector highlights its role in the generative AI boom.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $350.2 million. This reflects a revenue growth increase of nearly 46.9% over the previous year. The tech giant also achieved a net income of roughly $48.5 million during this period.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 2.7x. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating a strong balance sheet with no total debt. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $35.6 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.8% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    According to recent reports, bigBear.ai faces significant risk due to heavy revenue concentration with government customers who can terminate contracts for convenience. Scaling its sales efforts remains a challenge while managing long and unpredictable sales cycles. It also faces intense competition from Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) and Amazon (AMZN -4.10%). The firm also navigates complex AI deployment risks and recent financial volatility including litigation over accounting errors.

    Innodata relies heavily on a single customer that contributed nearly 58% of its 2025 revenues, making it vulnerable to contract changes. It competes against well-resourced firms like Accenture (ACN +1.19%) and Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH +3.11%) in the data engineering space. The business also deals with geopolitical risks from its global workforce and ongoing legal challenges regarding securities class actions.

    Innodata appears to offer a more attractive value proposition based on its lower P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    I'd go with Innodata. AI models are only as good as the data they learn from, and Innodata helps significant tech companies create and test that data. Its sales have grown year over year for 13 straight quarters, and it makes money.

    In a recent development, last quarter, sales jumped 53% and management raised its growth outlook, though the stock has fallen sharply this fall. There are risks: Two customers make up most of its sales, margins narrowed, and one program is winding down. But Innodata is adding new customers and work from a large cloud tech giant, and expects to replace the lost program by early next year.

    To give BigBear.ai its due, it does high-stakes work for national security and border security customers with contracts that are difficult to replace, and its backlog is growing. But it's still losing money, and government contract sales can be difficult to predict. That uncertainty is where Innodata stands apart: It is already profitable, with plenty of cash to keep investing as demand for AI data grows.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arizona Cardinals might be turning to their fourth quarterback of the season.
    • In a recent development, in a press conference, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur mentioned Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms and did not practice Friday.
    • "Not gonna shut the door on him [Beck], but we're gonna proceed as if Josh is gonna be starting on Sunday," LaFleur said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arizona Cardinals might be turning to their fourth quarterback of the season.

    In a recent development, in a press conference, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur mentioned Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms and did not practice Friday. As a result, the team is preparing for backup Josh Johnson to be the team's starting quarterback for Week 11.

    "Not gonna shut the door on him [Beck], but we're gonna proceed as if Josh is gonna be starting on Sunday," LaFleur said.

    Beck, who is a rookie, was thrust into the role of starter after Gardner Minshew went on injured reserve with a torn UCL. The Cardinals' original starter, Jacoby Brissett, was traded to the Baltimore Ravens after being benched for Minshew mid-game the week before.

    Beck was officially ruled as questionable in Friday's injury report.

    LaFleur noted in his press conference that the team will monitor how Beck responds to treatment and how he feels on Saturday before making any final decisions. The coach added that this is an concern that Beck has dealt with before, but wasn't able to provide a clear timeline for Beck's return.

    In the meantime, Johnson, who was signed off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad after the Minshew injury, looks poised to be stepping up for Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

    The itinerant backup quarterback also has some history with LaFleur: Johnson and LaFleur's careers overlapped in 2021, when both were with the Upcoming York Jets (LaFleur was an offensive coordinator at the time). LaFleur had high praise for Johnson, noting some of the reasons he's been able to keep his career going this long.

    According to recent reports, "If it is Josh, I've called plays for him before, and had a really great experience calling plays for him," LaFleur stated. "He is incredible in the quarterback room, he's incredible for the starters. He's incredible for young quarterbacks, in terms of the way he sees the game, his energy, his positivity, how he keeps it real. He's mature. And he can still sling it. … If that's the route that ends up happening, let's go.".

    Recent findings suggest that arizona is the 15th NFL franchise that Johnson has been a part of in his career, as the 40-year-old quarterback has bounced between half of the teams in the league. Across 16 seasons, he has only started 11 games in his NFL career.

    Negative sentiment from both its e-commerce and AWS segments seemed to weigh on Amazon stock today.

    Soft consumer spending and an increased need for promotional discounting led it to underperform retail counterparts like Walmart, which, as previously mentioned, rose in today's trading session.

    Moreover, capital expenditures (capex) continue to weigh on the stock. The firm's plan to spend $220 billion has led to free cash outflows, a concerning sign for a company that generated tens of billions in annual free cash flow until recently. Furthermore, despite a massive amount of liquidity, it has had to turn to the debt markets in a rising-rate environment.

    Such concerns were not unique to Amazon, and every stock in the Magnificent Seven, which contend with many of the same challenges, dropped today. Additionally, the Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) IPO has put AI in the spotlight this week. That stock has trended down since opening at $111.50 per share yesterday, likely adding to the negative sentiment surrounding AI.

    #16362. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1032 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1032 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • In a recent development, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    In a recent development, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    Sources indicate that spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    The high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he mentioned.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone stated.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That said, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, remarked Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    Sources indicate that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

    According to recent reports, the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, noted Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    In a recent development, in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she mentioned.

    Sources indicate that "It is isolated," she said. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she stated.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    Recent findings suggest that but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    Recent findings suggest that "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin noted. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    Sources indicate that it's also crucial to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, mentioned R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo noted.

    Sources indicate that "That's when spreads really widen out," he said. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    #16361. Here's the Average Social Security Benefit at Age 67

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (660 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Here's the Average Social Security Benefit at Age 67

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (660 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:00PM EST.
    • According to recent reports, the average Social Security benefit for 67-year-olds is $2,016.48 per month, according to Social Security Administration (SSA) data from December 2025.
    • Reaching this age doesn't always mean you receive exactly 100% of your baseline amount.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:00PM EST.

    According to recent reports, the average Social Security benefit for 67-year-olds is $2,016.48 per month, according to Social Security Administration (SSA) data from December 2025. Full retirement age (FRA) ranges from 66 to 67, depending on your birth year, and it's 67 for everyone born in 1960 or later. It's the point where you're eligible for your unreduced retirement amount.

    Reaching this age doesn't always mean you receive exactly 100% of your baseline amount. Many people who are 67 today have a full retirement age of 66 years and 10 months. These workers may have already earned small delayed retirement credits if they waited until 67 to claim their checks.

    According to recent reports, earnings histories also impact these averages. Men who are 67 receive an average of $2,234.41 per month, while the average among women is $1,801.82. This results in a monthly gender gap of $432.59 as of December 2025.

    Sources indicate that think of your full retirement age as the baseline for your benefits. The SSA bases your check on your average monthly income over your 35 highest-earning years, adjusting those wages for inflation and applying the primary insurance amount formula. This calculation creates the standard amount you're entitled to at full retirement age.

    It has been revealed that you don't have to claim at your baseline. You can earn delayed retirement credits, which are increases for delaying past FRA, worth 8% per year up to age 70. For a worker whose FRA is 67, waiting those three extra years provides a 24% total increase in monthly income.

    In a recent development, these decisions have a visible impact on the data. The average monthly benefit at age 70 is $2,274.68, which is $258.20 higher than the age-67 average.

    Sources indicate that but even for these claimants, benefits alone often aren't enough to live on. Social Security was only designed to replace about 40% of pre-retirement wages, so most retirees rely on savings or other income to cover their full costs.

    A 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) will take effect in 2027 to help benefits keep pace with inflation. This will add about $73 a month on top of the average listed above. These adjustments are designed to protect your purchasing power over time.

    Knowing the population average gives you a target for your own planning, but your final check depends on your career earnings and when you choose to claim.

    According to recent reports, waiting until age 67 to claim Social Security helps you avoid the early claiming benefit reduction, which can drastically reduce your checks. This is one major reason FRA is such a popular claiming age, but it's not the only one.

    When you claim Social Security under your FRA, you're also at risk of losing some of your benefits to the earnings test if you're still working. In 2027, for example, you lose $1 from your checks for every $2 you earn over $25,960 if you're under your FRA all year. If you'll reach your FRA next year, you only lose $1 for every $3 you earn over $67,920.

    These lost benefits come back to you as a permanent benefit boost at your FRA. But for some, the risk of short-term losses makes them delay their claim until their FRA, when the earnings test no longer applies. This is something to weigh if you proposal to continue working once you're eligible for Social Security checks.

    For more on how Social Security affects your retirement, see this guide.

    PayPal vs. SoFi Technologies: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (931 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 6:05PM EST.
    • Deciding between PayPal (PYPL -5.46%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%) requires balancing established market dominance against aggressive digital growth.
    • It has been revealed that payPal remains a global giant in payment processing, while SoFi is a fast-growing digital bank targeting a younger, high-earning demographic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 6:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than PayPal ›.

    Deciding between PayPal (PYPL -5.46%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -7.76%) requires balancing established market dominance against aggressive digital growth. Both companies are fighting for a larger share of your digital wallet today.

    It has been revealed that payPal remains a global giant in payment processing, while SoFi is a fast-growing digital bank targeting a younger, high-earning demographic. While they operate in different niches, both compete for the same pool of consumer financial activity, making them frequent candidates for a fintech-focused portfolio as investors look toward the future of money.

    PayPal operates a massive digital payments platform serving nearly 439 million active accounts across 200 markets. It provides branded checkout services, person-to-person payments via Venmo, and even Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) trading within its app. This scale makes it one of the most recognizable names in fintech stocks today as it adapts to a changing financial landscape.

    Reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each manufacturer's latest full fiscal year. For FY 2025, PayPal reported revenue of nearly $33.2 billion, representing growth of approximately 4.3% over the prior year. The company generated net income of close to $5.2 billion, showing a steady ability to convert its high volume of transactions into profit for its shareholders.

    In a recent development, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached roughly 0.5x, comparing total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, was approximately 1.3x. Free cash flow, or the cash remaining after paying for operations and equipment, was nearly $5.6 billion in FY 2025.

    Industry observers note that soFi Technologies is a mobile-first financial services provider that offers a wide range of products including student loan refinancing, home loans, and investment tools. It serves approximately 15.8 million members and has expanded into business services through a partnership with Mastercard (MA -0.14%). The firm also supports Bitcoin trading and provides modern banking infrastructure to other firms through its proprietary technology segments.

    For its latest annual report covering FY 2025, SoFi Technologies generated revenue of nearly $3.6 billion, which was an increase of approximately 35.1% compared to the previous year. The company reported net income of close to $481.3 million, marking a significant transition into consistent profitability. This growth was driven by a diversified mix of lending products and financial services that attracted fresh members to its platform.

    Sources indicate that based on its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.2x, helping investors see the low level of debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio was approximately 0.2x, which measures a company's ability to cover immediate liabilities with assets that can be quickly converted to cash. Free cash flow for the year was a net loss of nearly $4.0 billion, which often occurs in banking as capital is deployed into new loans rather than held as cash.

    PayPal faces intense competition from both traditional banks and newer technology platforms that offer digital checkout solutions. The manufacturer is also subject to extensive global regulatory oversight regarding payment processing and anti-money laundering rules. Any failure to manage cybersecurity risks or protect user data could lead to significant penalties and damage its reputation.

    SoFi Technologies must manage the complex regulatory requirements that come with being a bank holding company. It relies on a concentrated number of whole loan purchasers, meaning its results could suffer if these buyers reduce their activity. Additionally, the company faces the challenge of managing rapid growth across its various lending and technology segments without increasing credit risks.

    When comparing these two companies using Forward P/E, PayPal looks significantly cheaper than its peer based on future earnings estimates.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    Recent findings suggest that I'd go with SoFi Technologies. Its sales and earnings are both growing far faster than PayPal's, and it has built a full digital bank with more than 17 million members, starting from student loans. Its bank charter lets it fund loans with its members' deposits, a cost advantage most fintech rivals lack.

    According to recent reports, soFi also gave investors its 2027 outlook a full quarter early, and it came in above analysts' expectations, with revenue expected to grow about 27%. Management built it assuming interest rates keep rising, even after a rate hike this year hurt the stock. The shares are still down for the year, so long-term investors get a lower price for a profitable, growing business.

    In a recent development, to give PayPal its due, it is a household name that produces plenty of cash, and Venmo is growing fast. But its original business, letting shoppers pay online with their PayPal account, is barely growing, and overall sales are rising slowly. By contrast, SoFi's lending and banking businesses are surging, and even its technology business, which lost a large client, is expected to return to growth in 2027. For long-term investors, that mix of growth, profits, and a lower price makes SoFi the better buy for 2027.

    Prediction: Rocket Lab Will Triple Its Revenue by 2028. Here’s What That Would Mean for the Stock.

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business.
    • Except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't.
    • Industry observers note that rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

    Plenty of companies are growing incredibly well right now, including several from the artificial intelligence business. A company that's set to triple its top line over the course of the next couple of years, though? That seems outrageous.

    Except for orbital launch and satellite tech specialist Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%), it isn't. This future business is already lined up. These paying customers are just waiting for one pivotal milestone that's likely to materialize sometime next year. Then the floodgates open.

    Industry observers note that rocket Lab offers satellite launch solutions. Its relatively small Electron rocket design has now been rolled out 100 times, putting 273 satellites into low earth orbit.

    The organization also provides a range of satellite components and construction services, which accounts for more than half of last quarter's revenue of $268 million. Rocket Lab expects to do around $980 billion in business in fiscal 2026, well up from last year's $602 billion.

    This is just a taste of what's to come, though. As the firm confirmed with its third-quarter report posted earlier this month, Rocket Lab's backlog grew 52% from Q2's $2.36 billion to an incredible $3.6 billion. The organization just needs more capacity, but that's coming. Rocket Lab can now manufacture an Electron rocket every eight days.

    Sources indicate that then there's the proverbial 800-pound gorilla in the room. That's the manufacturer's larger Neutron rocket, which has seen its inaugural flight pushed back several times, with the first flight now expected sometime in 2027.

    Industry observers note that despite the delays so far, once Neutron is flying, everything takes a turn for the better. As CFO Adam Spice commented during the third-quarter's earnings conference call, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) "will turn positive within six months of that first successful test flight," with cash flow likely to turn positive shortly after that.

    According to recent reports, neutron isn't the big profit center in and of itself, to be clear. It's just a means to an end. Being able to put larger, heavier satellites into orbit also opens up its satellite tech business. Of its new backlog of $3.6 billion, $1.7 billion of it reflects space systems rather than launch services, up 194% year over year.

    Sources indicate that to this end, while analysts aren't yet looking for Rocket Lab's revenue to triple between now and 2028, with recent failures of similar rockets like ULA's Vulcan and one earlier in the year from Blue Origin, Rocket Lab is rapidly becoming a preferred launch option. It may well exceed 2028's expectations.

    It has been revealed that as for the impact on the stock, it's not a complicated prediction to make. If the company's top line comes anywhere close to tripling by 2028, the bullish argument firms up enormously.

    Industry observers note that while it may not triple in value in step with revenue, $3 billion in sales could turn this high-growth $34 billion outfit into a $60 billion outfit with relative ease. And given that the manufacturer isn't likely to raise money by issuing more stock anytime soon, that translates into a near-doubling of the stock's price.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    You're getting some help in the meantime, by the way. The analyst community overwhelmingly considers RKLB stock a strong buy right now, with a 12-month consensus price target of $93.30 already more than 80% above the ticker's current price.
